- If sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., 1.00) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -1.00) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — consider slight upward correction.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >75.00), forecast should not continue rising beyond 2–3 days — cap momentum to prevent overshoot.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00/0.25), model should not assume trend continuation — favor mean reversion toward recent 10–15 day average.  
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast in early days (e.g., first 5–7 days), adjust forecast downward if sentiment is negative or upward if sentiment is positive — apply early correction.  
- Forecast should not be more than 2 standard deviations above/below recent 18-day mean unless sentiment strongly supports it.  
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, forecast should begin to flatten or decline — avoid prolonged upward bias.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid linear extrapolation — incorporate sentiment decay and volatility clustering.
